incidents.victim: Al Jazeera, US DoD, NATO, IAEA, cybersecurity agencies (targeted)
incidents.attacker: Unknown — Israeli-linked mercenary spyware operators (Discover-Tech / Candiru)
incidents.vector: Zero-click spyware (Candiru) delivered silently through targeted online advertising via Discover-Tech's 'Controlium' ad platform, infecting devices the moment an ad renders on-screen without any user interaction
incidents.impact: At least 45 devices at Al Jazeera confirmed infected; Discover-Tech ads appeared on US DoD, NATO, IAEA, and world cybersecurity agency networks; campaign active since at least 2024; Discover-Tech removed from Google and IAB Europe vendor registries

incidents.victim: UK Legal Aid Agency
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data extortion
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited vulnerabilities in Legal Aid Agency IT systems to gain unauthorized access and exfiltrate decades of unstructured case management data
incidents.impact: ~250,000 records predating 2007 confirmed stolen including criminal histories, financial assessments, bank account and property details, probation records, and partially redacted payment card data; earliest record from 1978; UK government refuses to pay extortion demand

incidents.victim: Windows users (broad targeting, multiple sectors)
incidents.attacker: Unknown
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of Windows Shell security feature bypass (CVE-2026-96951) allowing attackers to send files that skip Mark of the Web warnings, enabling malware execution without user prompts
incidents.impact: Actively exploited in the wild; patched in October 2026 Patch Tuesday (1,413 total CVEs — highest ever monthly Microsoft release); CISA added to KEV Oct 13; third Windows Shell bypass exploited in 2026

incidents.victim: 75,000+ organizations globally (Japan, US, Australia, India)
incidents.attacker: China — criminal-linked phishing-as-a-service operators (Storm-3119, Storm-2990)
incidents.vector: Chinese-language YAM Store marketplace sold compromised Microsoft and Google cloud accounts alongside phishing kits (CoGUI, Haozi, Iron Man System) to operators who blasted over 1 billion phishing emails and SMS messages since January 2026
incidents.impact: 75,000+ organizations targeted; Microsoft seized marketplace domains via US federal court and disabled 20,000+ accounts; operations disrupted in coordination with Japan NPA, JC3, Health-ISAC, Resecurity, Cloudflare, Oracle, Proofpoint, and TRM Labs

incidents.victim: Multiple organizations (Ivanti Connect Secure VPN customers)
incidents.attacker: Unknown — likely state-linked espionage group (tracked by Volexity as UTA0576)
incidents.vector: Unauthenticated remote code execution via chained zero-days in Ivanti Connect Secure VPN (CVE-2026-104935); exploit chain bypasses authentication, executes code remotely, and escalates privileges; exploitation began Oct 1 before Ivanti issued a patch
incidents.impact: Confirmed post-exploitation includes credential theft, Active Directory metadata dump, custom tool deployment, log tampering, and network reconnaissance; CISA warns Integrity Checker Tool cannot detect memory-only exploitation; widespread exploitation expected given history of Ivanti targeting

incidents.victim: Ledger hardware cryptocurrency wallet customers (CryptoBilis reseller, Asia and Europe)
incidents.attacker: Unknown — suspected Chinese-linked group (CryptoBilis acquired by undisclosed Chinese company)
incidents.vector: Spy chips (LTE modem with eSIM) professionally soldered into Ledger Nano X and Flex hardware wallets by a rogue reseller, intercepting seed phrases from the device display before transmitting them over cellular to attackers
incidents.impact: $86–100 million in cryptocurrency stolen; Ledger recalled all CryptoBilis-sourced devices; customers advised to immediately move funds to new wallet addresses; implants found in devices sold in Southeast Asia and at MediaMarkt stores in Europe

incidents.victim: 70+ US companies (aerospace, energy, financial services, healthcare, cybersecurity, defense, technology)
incidents.attacker: North Korea — state-sponsored, financially motivated (DPRK 313 General Bureau)
incidents.vector: DPRK-controlled IT workers used stolen identities and US-hosted laptop farms maintained by paid American facilitators to covertly hold remote jobs, exfiltrate data, and extort employers; Operation Lonestar Roundup
incidents.impact: 14 individuals charged including 2 US citizen facilitators; 40+ Texas laptop farms seized; 187+ computers confiscated; ~$3M in salary diverted to DPRK weapons programs; scheme persists through subcontracting to freelancers in South Asia and West Africa

incidents.victim: Foschini Group UK (Phase Eight, Hobbs, Whistles)
incidents.attacker: Unknown — criminal likely (part of wave targeting UK fashion retail)
incidents.vector: Undisclosed attack vector; IT systems taken offline as a containment measure shortly after discovery
incidents.impact: IT systems at three UK fashion brands disrupted; online orders delayed; South African and Australian operations unaffected due to separate IT infrastructure; investigation and forensics ongoing

incidents.victim: Ahold Delhaize (Food Lion, Stop & Shop, Albert Heijn, Etos, Gall & Gall, Delhaize, Profi, Mega Image)
incidents.attacker: Unknown
incidents.vector: Cyberattack of undisclosed nature; Ahold Delhaize proactively took systems offline across multiple subsidiary brands to limit potential damage
incidents.impact: Online grocery orders, distribution center operations, and in-store electronic pricing disrupted across US, Netherlands, Belgium, and Romania; operations affecting over 400,000 employees; prior 2024 breach of same company stole 2.2 million customer records

incidents.victim: OpenAI
incidents.attacker: Unknown — Saudi Arabia intelligence-linked (implied by DOJ framing and meeting topics captured)
incidents.vector: Saudi national employee installed a covert audio recording device concealed inside a USB port in OpenAI's executive conference room, capturing high-level meetings
incidents.impact: Meetings covering AI technology, product plans, and government engagements recorded over an unknown period; device discovered September 30 and arrested October 13; full extent of captured intelligence unknown

incidents.victim: Multiple organizations (Cisco Firepower Management Console customers)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — ransomware (Qilin group, with separate espionage actors also exploiting same flaws)
incidents.vector: Three separate threat groups exploited CVE-2026-20079 and CVE-2026-20316 in Cisco Firepower Management Console for credential theft, webshell installation, Cyclops Blink-style persistent malware, and Qilin ransomware deployment
incidents.impact: Multiple organizations breached via their core network security management platform; Qilin ransomware deployed in at least one campaign; persistent backdoors installed; a Qilin member was subsequently arrested in Japan

incidents.victim: FBI (US federal law enforcement), Boeing spin-off (extortion target)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data extortion (ShinyHunters)
incidents.vector: ShinyHunters breached FBI data infrastructure and stole personnel records; separately extorted a Boeing spin-off company using stolen data as leverage
incidents.impact: FBI employee data including sensitive intelligence role information stolen; Boeing spin-off extorted; ShinyHunters leader 'Rey' arrested in Jordan and cooperating with authorities; Dutch member arrested separately

incidents.victim: Meta (Facebook parent company)
incidents.attacker: Unknown — criminal likely
incidents.vector: Threat actor used stolen employee credentials to access Meta's GitHub repositories and exfiltrate employee data and source code
incidents.impact: Personal data of 1,500+ US employees stolen including some proprietary source code; Meta notified all affected personnel; breach occurred in September 2026 and disclosed in October

incidents.victim: Hundreds of French supermarkets (primarily Intermarché chain)
incidents.attacker: Unknown
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited internet-connected Danfoss refrigeration units running outdated firmware with default credentials, triggering defrost cycles and raising freezer and refrigerator temperatures to 50°C
incidents.impact: Tens of millions of euros in food stock destroyed overnight across hundreds of locations; widespread food supply disruption; ACSC issued alert warning Australian operators of similar OT refrigeration risks

incidents.victim: Government, critical manufacturing, healthcare, IT, law enforcement, education organizations globally
incidents.attacker: China — Integrity Technology Group-enabled state actors (Chinese government-linked)
incidents.vector: AI-enabled automated scanning combined with large-scale botnets and hands-on exploitation by Chinese state actors enabled through Integrity Technology Group's infrastructure, tooling, and personnel
incidents.impact: Ongoing global compromise of critical sector networks and sensitive data theft; joint advisory from NSA, FBI, NCSC, and partners from Australia, Canada, Japan, New Zealand, Spain; actor TTPs overlap with Flax Typhoon, Storm 919, Ethereal Panda, and Red Juliett campaigns; Integrity Tech sanctioned by UK

incidents.victim: ASOS (UK online fashion retailer and its customers)
incidents.attacker: Unknown — criminal likely (part of coordinated wave targeting UK fashion retailers)
incidents.vector: Attacker compromised an ASOS employee account by impersonating a trusted contact, then used access to send unauthorized push notifications to customers and access personal records
incidents.impact: Customer names and contact details accessed for potentially all ASOS customers; payment card information and account passwords not believed compromised; NCSC issued public guidance; part of broader wave also targeting H&M and Foschini Group UK brands

incidents.victim: Telecom managed service provider and 500+ downstream managed FortiGate firewall clients
incidents.attacker: Unknown — nation-state level tradecraft (tracked as CL-STA-0954 / UNC5820)
incidents.vector: Initial access via CVE-2024-47575 (FortiJump); privilege escalation via CVE-2025-61624; novel memory-resident ARM64 PEERSTITCH malware communicates exclusively through legitimate process traffic with no listening ports or outbound connections to evade detection
incidents.impact: Firewall configurations for 500+ client organizations exfiltrated; PEERSTITCH implant designed to survive standard detection; downstream MSP clients face significant lateral exposure risk

incidents.victim: 395 organizations (440 PaperCut print management instances)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — Russian-speaking, AI-augmented
incidents.vector: AI agents deployed to automate mass exploitation of PaperCut NG/MF print management vulnerabilities CVE-2026-81578 and CVE-2026-82078 across hundreds of organizations simultaneously
incidents.impact: 440 PaperCut instances compromised across 395 organizations; AI-augmented exploitation enabled attack scale and speed far exceeding traditional campaigns; full downstream impact under investigation

incidents.victim: 49+ organizations (WordPress), 11 critical infrastructure organizations (Gitea), others
incidents.attacker: China — state-suspected espionage group (Red Heron)
incidents.vector: Opportunistic mass exploitation of CVE-2026-63030 (WordPress RCE) and CVE-2026-60004 (Gitea) alongside Linux kernel and Proxmox vulnerabilities to establish persistent footholds for data collection
incidents.impact: Persistent access established across 60+ organizations including 11 critical infrastructure targets; source code repositories and databases exfiltrated; credential harvesting ongoing; campaign active since May 2026

incidents.victim: 153 million+ US and Canadian residents (via Louisiana identity verification company)
incidents.attacker: Unknown — criminal
incidents.vector: Criminal actor exfiltrated driver's license images and associated records from a Louisiana-based identity verification company and launched a dark web service selling the stolen data
incidents.impact: Over 153 million US and Canadian driver's license images and personal records offered for sale on the dark web; FBI investigation launched; massive identity fraud and impersonation risk for affected populations

incidents.victim: US Embassy, Suva, Fiji
incidents.attacker: China — state-linked espionage group
incidents.vector: Network intrusion maintaining persistent unauthorized access to the US Embassy's IT systems over a two-month period
incidents.impact: Chinese hackers maintained access to US Embassy Fiji network from July to August 2026; US government notified Fiji authorities; Fiji government networks potentially also targeted during the same period

incidents.victim: CIS government organizations (Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Russia, Belarus)
incidents.attacker: Unknown — Kazakhstan-nexus espionage group (medium confidence; also tracked as Silent Lynx / YoroTrooper cluster)
incidents.vector: Macro-enabled documents, PS2EXE obfuscation, GitHub-hosted PowerShell command-and-control, and WinRAR vulnerability CVE-2025-8088 used to collect diplomatic, economic, and energy intelligence from nine Central Asian and post-Soviet governments
incidents.impact: 15-month intelligence collection campaign across nine countries targeting diplomatic, economic, and energy information; campaign concluded August 2026 and attributed with medium confidence to a Kazakhstan-nexus actor

incidents.victim: Russian companies (Microsoft Exchange server operators)
incidents.attacker: Unknown — suspected Western or Ukraine-aligned espionage group
incidents.vector: Compromised VPN credentials provided initial access; Exchange crypto keys extracted to modify VIEWSTATE and deploy GhostContainer backdoor; CVE-2019-0708 (BlueKeep RDP) exploited for lateral movement to unpatched legacy systems
incidents.impact: Persistent GhostContainer backdoor deployed on Exchange servers of multiple Russian organizations; ongoing email intelligence collection; exploitation of BlueKeep indicates continued exposure of unpatched legacy Windows systems within targeted environments
